own_solution.law: Continuity gives v_throat = 4 v_wide. The differential manometer gives Δp = (ρ_m − ρ)gh. Horizontal Bernoulli gives Δp = ρ(v_throat² − v_wide²)/2 = 15ρv_wide²/2. Thus Q = (πD_wide²/4)sqrt[2(ρ_m − ρ)gh/(15ρ)]. With the original manometer liquid, Δp = 14817.6 Pa.
assumptions: The manometer liquid is in hydrostatic equilibrium when read.
The horizontal sections have equal elevation.
The stated steady, incompressible, frictionless flow model applies.
A replacement before reading makes the stated 12 cm difference refer to the replacement liquid; an earlier-experiment-only replacement leaves the present liquid unchanged.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The density variants do not preserve numerical specificity: T90FF and T5A70 state only that the density is known, whereas their corresponding variants T2C4F and T6113 explicitly state 2500 kg/m³.

notes: The base physics and all individual augmented problems are solvable; the invalid verdict concerns the required minimal-variant property. Omitting a numerical density in T90FF and T5A70 does not make their individual answers indeterminate because those replacements are disconnected from the current measurement. With a current U-tube density of 2500 kg/m³, Δp = 1764 Pa and Q = 0.003809 m³/s. Absolute pressure cancels when Bernoulli is differenced, and the common pipe elevation cancels from the gravitational terms. The chronological replacement statements are compatible with the original liquid specification.
